001: Haoran, do you have time this afternoon? I want to go to the office to see the professor.
I'm free. I'll go with you. What do you want to talk to the professor about?
I want to ask if I can change the topic for the midterm paper.
Changing the topic might be a bit troublesome. You'd better think of a reason in advance.
I've already thought of one. I'll just say I don't understand the original topic well enough.
Okay then. I'll wait for you downstairs at your dorm at two.
002: Professor, is it convenient for you right now? I'd like to ask a few questions.
Sure, come in and have a seat. Feel free to ask whatever you want.
When I'm writing my paper, I'm not sure which research method I should use.
That depends on what your research question is. What specific aspect do you want to study?
I want to study the influence of social media on college students' spending habits.
Then you could try a questionnaire survey. The data would be easier to collect.
003: Professor, did you get a chance to look at my homework from last week? I'd like to hear your thoughts.
I did. Overall it's good, but the conclusion part was written a bit hastily.
I also feel the conclusion isn't strong enough, but I don't know how to fix it.
You can organize your arguments again, and then summarize based on the data.
Okay, I'll go back and revise it, and bring you another version next week.
Sure. Once you've revised it, feel free to email it to me anytime.
004: Professor, I want to apply for the exchange program next semester, and I need a letter of recommendation.
No problem. I'd be happy to write one for you. Which school are you planning to go to?
I want to go to a university in Beijing. The program there fits my major better.
Beijing is a good choice. When do you need the letter by?
I just need to submit it by the tenth of next month. Thank you for your help.
There's enough time. Just remind me when the time comes.
005: Professor, I've been having trouble keeping up in class lately. The content feels harder and harder.
Which part exactly do you find difficult? Is it the theory or the practice?
It's mainly the theory part. I can't remember a lot of the concepts, and I can't tell them apart.
I suggest you organize your notes once a week and make comparison tables for the concepts.
That sounds like a good method. I'll give it a try.
If you still have problems, feel free to come to my office anytime.
006: Professor, I'd like to hear your advice on choosing a topic for my graduation thesis.
First, tell me what area you're interested in, and then I'll help you analyze it.
I'm quite interested in urban transportation planning, but I feel the scope is too broad.
It is indeed too broad. You can narrow it down to a specific district in a specific city.
Then can I choose the area around our campus to study?
Sure. That scope is more appropriate, and the materials are easier to find.
007: Professor, I didn't do well on the last exam, and I feel a bit upset about it.
One exam doesn't mean anything. What matters is what you learned from it.
I think the main problem was my study method. I only read the textbook and didn't do practice problems.
Then adjust your approach this time. Do more past exam questions from previous years.
Okay, I'll prepare well this time and try to do better on the next one.
I believe in you. Come to me anytime you need help.
008: Professor, I'd like to ask how the final grade for this course is calculated.
Class participation counts for thirty percent, the midterm is thirty percent, and the final is forty percent.
Does speaking up in class count toward the participation grade?
Yes, it does. I record every time you speak, so you should participate more.
Got it. Then I'll try to speak up in every class from now on.
Great. Being more active can only benefit you.
009: Professor, I've been working on a research project recently, and I'd like to get some advice from you.
First, give me a brief introduction to your research plan.
I plan to hand out questionnaires first, and then do in-depth interviews with a few students.
The approach is good, but the design of the questionnaire questions needs to be more specific.
Then I'll go back and refine the questions, and send them to you once they're done.
Okay. I'll give you feedback after I look at them.
010: Professor, I'd like to learn about the course schedule for next semester in advance.
Next semester I'm teaching two courses. One is required, and one is elective.
What is the elective course about? I'd like to read up on it in advance.
It's mainly about the history of urban development. You can start by reading some introductory books on the topic.
Okay. Could you recommend one or two books?
I'll send the book list to the course group later. Keep an eye out for it.
